messages:
jess: quick q — contractor (optimetrics) needs to look at recent error logs in project redwood-prod to debug a payments issue. Do they need Project Viewer? I want to avoid broad perms. Any preferred flow? @marta

marta (sec): don't give Project Viewer. Create a custom role scoped to logging read for the specific service/log bucket. Grant only `logEntries.list`/`logs.viewer` equivalent and restrict to the service account or log names. Also consider redacting PII in the sample logs before sharing.

liam (infra): +1. We have an access-bot flow for temporary grants — open an access request in #access-requests and the bot can issue a 4h `logging.viewer` on the project for a specific principal. That avoids long-lived perms.

kevin (sre): agree with custom role. If they need traces/stackdriver links, only add trace viewer for that service resource. Also double-check exported logs (BigQuery/s3) ACLs — don't accidentally expose copies.

marta (sec): for redaction: prefer structured logs with user_id hashed and remove full emails/phone numbers. If you paste a tiny sample (sanitized) into the ticket I can run a quick scan and suggest redaction rules or scrub it before we grant access.

jess: cool. i'll create a ticket with a sanitized sample and request temporary access via access-bot. plan: custom role scoped to `redwood-ingest` service logs + 4h temp grant for contractor@optimetrics.com. tagging @kevin to confirm export ACLs.

access-bot: access-bot: Temporary role `roles/logging.viewer` granted to contractor@optimetrics.com for 4 hours on project redwood-prod (requested by jess). :white_check_mark:

jess: closing the loop — contractor confirmed they could reproduce and debug, no PII in the sample. I'll follow up to provision a read-only service account if they need longer-term access. Thanks everyone :tada:
